content: Constipation is a very common condition in children and can result in overflow soiling or encopresis. In severe cases, the standard treatment involves clearing the bowels of impacted stool using oral or rectal laxatives. Following this, regular bowel movements are maintained through the continued use of osmotic and stimulant laxatives. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of stimulant laxatives in treating chronic constipation in children, particularly in those who also experience soiling or encopresis. To gather relevant data, the Cochrane database of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was searched. Additional references were sought by manually reviewing pediatric journals and consulting with professionals in the field. The review aimed to include all RCTs that compared the use of stimulant laxatives in children to either a placebo or alternative treatments. However, no trials were identified that met the inclusion criteria. As a result, no data from eligible trials were available for analysis. The authors concluded that there is a significant need for well-designed and adequately powered trials to provide reliable comparative data on the effectiveness of commonly used stimulant laxatives in children. This would help establish a stronger evidence base for treatment decisions.
